hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever looked after something that wasn’t yours? a friend’s plant, a pet, a house?
options: then you know what today’s word feels like.
that’s honest. even the angels had questions. listen.
that’s okay. today, the first job ever given.

steps.line: The first story doesn’t start on earth. It starts in a conversation. God tells the angels: “I am placing a steward on the earth.”

steps.q: The angels, who only ever praise God, answer. What do you think they say?
o: “What will this steward be made of?”
“Will You place one who’ll do harm?”
“Will it praise You as we do?”
steps.why: They worry about harm and bloodshed, and say it openly (2:30). Not a protest, many scholars say: an honest question.

steps.line: The angels ask: “Will You place there one who will cause harm and shed blood, while we praise You?”
God doesn’t scold them. He says only: “I know what you do not know.”

steps.q: Why does it matter that the angels were allowed to ask?
o: It shows an honest question isn’t rebellion
It shows the angels doubted God
It shows God changed His plan
steps.why: Even the angels asked, and were answered, not punished. An honest question has a place in faith.

steps.q: How did the angels know a new creature might shed blood? Some classical commentators offer an answer. Which?
o: They had seen it in a dream
Jinn had lived on earth first, and done harm
steps.why: Commentators like al-Tabari report that jinn lived on earth first and spread bloodshed. Others say God had told the angels. The Qur’an itself doesn’t say.

steps.line: The word is khalifah: one who stands in for another. Not the owner of the garden. The one it’s entrusted to.
A saying puts it plainly: the world is sweet and green, and God has made you stewards in it, to see how you act.

steps.q: You’re holding a sapling when the end of the world begins. A famous saying tells you what to do. What?
steps.why: “If the Hour comes and one of you has a sapling in hand, let him plant it” (Musnad Ahmad). A steward keeps tending to the very last minute.

steps.line: Today, a mother and son plant a sapling in the park. A saying teaches: whatever any creature eats from it counts as charity.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. the angels asked a hard question, and God answered gently: i know what you do not know.
in islam, people are placed on the earth as khalifah: entrusted, not owners. the world is a trust, and the test is how you treat it.

steps.q: The angels asked about harm, and God said, “I know what you do not know.” What does that answer suggest?
o: There’s more in people than harm
steps.why: Harm was possible, and God didn’t deny it. But there was more to see. Tomorrow, He shows them.

today.say: today, tend one small piece of the trust: water a street tree, pick up litter on your block, or turn off what doesn’t need to be on. a saying teaches that whatever a bird or person eats from what you plant counts as charity.
options: lovely. that’s the steward’s whole job.
beautiful. it keeps giving after you’ve gone.

sources: Qur’an 2:30 (“Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not,” Pickthall)
Sahih Muslim 2742 (the world is sweet and green, and Allah is making you successors in it to see how you act)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2320; Sahih Muslim 1553 (no Muslim plants a tree or sows a crop and a bird, person or animal eats from it, but it is charity for him)
Root kh-l-f (to come after, to succeed, to stand in for): Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon
check: Commentators differ on khalifah: a successor (to earlier beings on earth) or one who stands in on God’s behalf; “steward, one entrusted” follows the script. Confirm.
